info.title: BlindSpot Backend
info.description:
Requirements-driven product validation. A product manager imports requirements
from their own documents, approves what the product is supposed to do, and
BlindSpot runs those requirements against the real application in a browser.

Every verdict comes back with the evidence behind it, and anything a model
inferred stays visibly separate from what was actually observed.

get.description: Server-sent events. Reconnect with Last-Event-ID to replay what was missed; refetch the run on completion rather than trusting the stream alone.
Pending is not zero. Cost may arrive after a run finishes and is final only once everything expected has.
Redirects to a short-lived signed URL. Evidence is served by id, never by storage path.

post.description: Deduplicated on event_id and ordered by sequence. Persisted before being published to the live stream.
Idempotent on usage_id. A revision replaces an estimate rather than adding a second charge.
Cost becomes final only when the reported usage count matches. Run completion alone is not sufficient.

usage_id.title: Usage Id
usage_id.description: Deduplication key. A retry must not add a second charge.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: A revision replaces an estimate; it does not add to it.

id.title: Id
id.description: Omit to create a new criterion.

Acknowledged.title: Acknowledged
Acknowledged.description: Returned by endpoints that accept work rather than complete it.

CostFinalization.title: CostFinalization
CostFinalization.description: Run completion alone is not sufficient — usage can arrive afterwards.

CriterionAssessment.title: CriterionAssessment
CriterionAssessment.description:
`source` is what lets the frontend render model output differently from
observed fact. A deterministic check outranks a model judgement.

DashboardCounts.title: DashboardCounts
DashboardCounts.description:
Coverage counts the latest result per requirement, so running the same
requirement repeatedly does not inflate it. `inconclusive` is derived as
tested - passed - failed; `untested` stays distinct.

Environment.title: Environment
Environment.description:
Credentials are never present on this model. The response says whether
they are set, not what they are.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.description: Write-only. Stored encrypted and never returned.

EnvironmentUpdate.title: EnvironmentUpdate
EnvironmentUpdate.description:
Changing base_url clears verified_at and bumps revision, which
invalidates any saved plan built against the old target.

message.title: Message
examples: Not yet implemented. Requirements CRUD lands in B4.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: Every error response in this API. Never a raw exception string.

event_id.title: Event Id
event_id.description: Deduplication key. A retry must not create a second row.

ImportResult.title: ImportResult
ImportResult.description:
Everything an import produced. Requirements land as drafts; nothing is
auto-approved.

LatestResult.title: LatestResult
LatestResult.description:
The most recent completed result for this requirement. Null until
something has run. Approval is reported separately and does not imply a
requirement passed.

role.title: Role
role.description: The caller's role in this project.

ProjectUpdate.title: ProjectUpdate
ProjectUpdate.description:
A project carries only a name and description. The application's URL
lives on an environment, not here.

RequirementSnapshot.title: RequirementSnapshot
RequirementSnapshot.description: Frozen when the run was queued, so history survives later edits.

RequirementSource.title: RequirementSource
RequirementSource.description:
Provenance. For an imported requirement the excerpt is real source text
the server selected — not model prose — so a reviewer can check it.

RequirementUpdate.title: RequirementUpdate
RequirementUpdate.description:
Sending `acceptance_criteria` REPLACES the whole set — the server
reconciles by id in one transaction. Editing title, description or criteria
resets approval_status to draft.

Result.title: Result
Result.description:
One requirement, one run. `observed_behavior` is plain-English fact;
model reasoning lives in the per-criterion rationales.

engine.title: Engine
engine.description: Which engine produced this run. Recorded so results stay comparable.

RunCreate.title: RunCreate
RunCreate.description: Only approved requirements may be selected, at most ten per run.
